newsitem.title: USA: Boat launched to recreate Viking explorer's voyage.
newsitem.headline: Boat launched to recreate Viking explorer's voyage.

text.p: Author-adventurer W. Hodding Carter floated a step closer to reliving history on Saturday, launching the boat he hopes will retrace Viking Leif Ericsson's voyage to North America.
A crowd of several hundred people who had lined the rocky shore of a coastal inlet cheered as the replica of a wood 54- foot (16 metre) Viking knarr was lifted off its cradle by the rising tide.

"It's a way of, I hope, bringing history alive," said Carter, who plans this summer to chronicle the 1,900-mile (3,000 km) route Ericsson took in the year 1000 from Greenland to Labrador and Newfoundland.
Ericsson, who was known as "Leif the Lucky", was the first of several Viking sailors to set foot on North America, making his trip nearly 500 years before Christopher Columbus set sail.
Carter, 34, who has already retraced and written about the journeys of several U.S. historical figures, said he has been inspired by the adventure and historical books he read as a boy.
Carter said it was difficult to find detailed design information about the knarr, a cargo craft used by Viking merchants and explorers who travelled the seas in search of settlement land.

"It isn't the long ship that everyone envisions with dragon heads ... it's really a good work boat is what it is," said Carter, who named the craft "Snorri" in honour of the first Viking child born in Newfoundland.
The open-deck boat is powered by single sail and six oars. It will not have a engine, but will carry a radio, electronic positioning equipment and crew survival suits in case of an emergency.
The project's cost of more than $500,000 is being largely underwritten by retailer Lands' End - which will publish a series of Carter's stories from the voyage in its upcoming catalogues.
The boat's 12-member crew will train for several weeks off the Maine coast before the boat is sent by container ship to Greenland. Carter hopes to arrive in eastern Canada in mid August.
